title: The Back Door at Ten
subtitle: 酒吧与社交 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 酒吧与社交（社会服务与人际沟通·社交与场所）
meta: 主题语境：酒吧与社交（社会服务与人际沟通·社交与场所）　|　核心词汇：bar　|　正文 328 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 bar 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 my uncle was put out of ① a bar for the first time and said the walk home was the interesting part. The ② bar, meaning the room and not the drink, had nine tables and one clock that was always eleven; a bar, he said, is the only public place where everybody has agreed on the subject before they arrive.

Every ③ bar in that street closed at ten, and the ④ bar at the end, meaning the one with the back door and not either of those, stayed open for anybody who knew the knock. A bar, my grandmother said, is nine parts company and one part somebody who can listen; my uncle said the company does the damage.

My mother meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ bar was the whole of the door, meaning the bolt and not the room. The ⑥ bar, meaning the piece of metal and not any of that, is the only thing in a house that is honest about what it is for; a bar, she said, is either a room you are put out of or the only word that means both a latch and a place. He said the latch came first.

By 1970 the ⑦ bar had become a club with a sign, and the sign had become an argument about who was allowed in. The ⑧ bar of the whole thing, my uncle wrote in June, was nine years of company and one door; a bar, he said, is either the room at the end of the street or the reason you learned the knock. She said the knock was the part that mattered.

The ⑨ bar I remember is the back door, which was never locked and never used after 1972. A ⑩ bar, my mother said in 1975, is the only place that improves by being closed; every bar, she said, is a bolt that has agreed to look like a room. He said the bolt was always the point.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 酒吧（指那个房间，与酒相对）
C. 固定搭配：be put out of a bar 被赶出酒吧
D. n. 酒吧（指那条街上每一家）
E. n. 酒吧（指尽头那一家）
G. n. 门闩（抽象：那块金属）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a bar for the first time
The bar, meaning the room and not the drink
bar was the whole of the door
The bar, meaning the piece of metal
the bar had become a club with a sign
The bar of the whole thing
A bar, my mother said in 1975

answers.why: be put out of a bar 意为“被赶出酒吧”，1958 年叔叔第一次被人从酒吧里赶了出来。
bar 意为“酒吧”，指那个房间而不是酒，有九张桌子和一只永远指着十一点的钟。
bar 指那条街上每一家酒吧，那条街上每一家都是十点关门。
bar 指尽头那一家酒吧（有后门的那一间），对知道怎么敲门的人一直开着。
bar 意为“门闩、横杆”，母亲说 bar 就是那扇门的全部，指的是门闩而不是那个房间。
bar 为抽象用法，指那块金属，是一栋房子里唯一对自己用途毫不掩饰的东西。
bar 意为“酒吧”，到 1970 年这个 bar 成了一家挂招牌的俱乐部。
bar 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，叔叔六月写道，整件事权衡下来是九年的陪伴和一扇门。
bar 意为“酒吧（那扇后门）”，我记得的是那扇后门，1972 年之后再没人用过。
bar 为抽象总称，母亲说酒吧是唯一会因为关门而变得更好的地方。

那家酒吧，指的是那个房间而不是酒，有九张桌子和一只永远指着十一点的钟。（bar）
那条街上每一家酒吧十点关门。（bar）
尽头那家酒吧，指的是有后门的那一间，对知道怎么敲门的人一直开着。（bar）
母亲说 bar 就是那扇门的全部，指的是门闩而不是那个房间。（bar）
1975 年母亲说，酒吧是唯一会因为关门而变得更好的地方。（bar）

The bar, meaning the room and not the drink, had nine tables and one clock that was always eleven.
Every bar in that street closed at ten.
The bar at the end, meaning the one with the back door and not either of those, stayed open for anybody who knew the knock.
My mother said bar was the whole of the door, meaning the bolt and not the room.
A bar, my mother said in 1975, is the only place that improves by being closed.
